After a `202`, sipnab polls its `Location` for the receipt within `--vcon-forward-timeout`, honoring `Retry-After`, and only on the scheme, host and port of this URL (draft-ietf-scitt-scrapi-11 section 2.4); the record marks a receipt still running then as `pending`. What the service answered goes into `<name>.scitt` beside the delivered container. sipnab logs and records a statement that does not register, and does not retry it; the delivery stands. Needs `--vcon-forward-scitt-sign-key`, `--vcon-forward-scitt-sign-cert` and `--vcon-forward-scitt-issuer`, each from its flag or its key; without one sipnab refuses the run with exit `2`, naming it. More: [Register lifecycle statements with a transparency service](@/docs/vcon.md#register-lifecycle-statements-with-a-transparency-service). Config: `[vcon_forward] scitt_url` |
| `--vcon-forward-scitt-auth-file` | `<FILE>` | -- | 0.5.219 | File holding one `Header-Name: value` line sent with each registration. Refused when other users can read it (`chmod 600` it). The store's credential never goes to the transparency service, and this one never goes to the store. Config: `[vcon_forward] scitt_auth_file` |
| `--vcon-forward-scitt-ca` | `<FILE>` | host bundle | 0.5.219 | Trust only the CA certificates in this PEM file for an `https://` transparency service. Config: `[vcon_forward] scitt_ca` |
| `--vcon-forward-scitt-sign-key` | `<FILE>` | -- | 0.5.219 | The PEM private key that signs the statements: an RSA key signs RS256 (COSE `alg` -257), an EC P-256 key ES256 (`alg` -7). The same kinds of key an encrypting `[[vcon.rule]]` names in `sign_key`. Refused when other users can read it (`chmod 600` it), with exit `2`; the same file named by `[vcon_forward] scitt_sign_key` exits `1`. Config: `[vcon_forward] scitt_sign_key` |
| `--vcon-forward-scitt-sign-cert` | `<FILE>` | -- | 0.5.219 | The PEM certificate chain of the signing key, leaf first, carried in each statement's `x5chain`. sipnab refuses a chain whose first certificate is not the key's before it sends anything, naming both flags, with exit `2` (`1` when `[vcon_forward] scitt_sign_key` named the key). Config: `[vcon_forward] scitt_sign_cert` |
| `--vcon-forward-scitt-issuer` | `<URI>` | -- | 0.5.219 | The issuer each statement names in its CWT Claims (`iss`): a URI of 1 to 8192 characters, such as `https://pbx.example.com/sipnab`. Config: `[vcon_forward] scitt_issuer` |
| `--vcon-forward-content-type` | `<TYPE>` | `application/json` | 0.5.219 | The `Content-Type` of a JSON container: `application/json`, `application/vcon+json` or `application/vcon`. A gzip format container always goes as `application/vcon+gzip`, the type draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04 section 5.4 names, whatever this says. Choose `application/vcon` only for a store you know accepts it. See [What it does with each container](@/docs/vcon.md#what-it-does-with-each-container). Config: `[vcon_forward] content_type` |
| `--vcon-spool-status` | `<SPOOL_DIR>` | -- | 0.5.212 | Print the state of an `--export-vcon-dir` spool as JSON and exit: containers pending, delivered and failed, and the `<name>.error.json` record beside each failed container. Reads the forwarder's default `delivered/` and `failed/` directories beside the spool. A snapshot of the files: it sends, moves, creates and deletes nothing. The MCP tool `vcon_spool_status` and `GET /v1/vcon/spool` give the same answer. Exit `0` after printing, also for a spool directory that does not exist yet, `1` when sipnab cannot read a directory that exists. Refused beside any capture flag, `--vcon-forward` and `--vcon-fetch` |

**Examples**

- `sipnab --vcon-forward spool --vcon-forward-url 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/vcon/external-ingress?ingress_list=sipnab' --vcon-forward-auth-file vcon-forward.auth --vcon-forward-once` — deliver what is in `spool` to a self-hosted conserver's `sipnab` ingress list once, and exit `0` when the conserver accepted all of it
- `sipnab --vcon-forward spool --vcon-forward-kind vcon-store --vcon-forward-url https://api.vcon.store --vcon-forward-auth-file vcon-store.key` — keep delivering to vcon.store until stopped: the kind adds `/v1/vcons`, and sends the key in the file as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`
- `sipnab --vcon-forward spool --vcon-forward-kind conserver --vcon-forward-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --vcon-forward-auth-file conserver.key --vcon-forward-once` — deliver to a self-hosted conserver's `sipnab` ingress list once: the kind adds `/vcon/external-ingress?ingress_list=sipnab` and sends the key as `x-conserver-api-token`
- `sipnab --vcon-forward spool --config /etc/sipnab/vcon-store.toml` — take every forwarder setting from a config file's `[vcon_forward]` section
- `sipnab --vcon-forward spool --vcon-forward-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/vcons --vcon-forward-auth 'Authorization: Bearer test-token' --vcon-forward-once` — a test against a store on this machine, with the credential on the command line, where every user of the host can read it in the process list; for anything else, export `SIPNAB_VCON_FORWARD_AUTH` instead
- `sipnab --vcon-forward spool --vcon-forward-kind conserver --vcon-forward-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --vcon-forward-auth test-key --vcon-forward-once` — the same with a bare key, which the `conserver` kind sends as `x-conserver-api-token: test-key`
- `sipnab --vcon-forward spool --vcon-forward-url https://vcon.example.com/v1/vcons --vcon-forward-auth-file vcon.auth --vcon-forward-backoff-first 10 --vcon-forward-backoff-cap 600` — a store that recovers slowly: wait 10 s after the first failed try, doubling to at most 10 minutes
- `sipnab --vcon-forward spool --vcon-forward-url https://vcon.example.com/v1/vcons --vcon-forward-auth-file vcon.auth --vcon-forward-backoff-first 1 --vcon-forward-backoff-cap 30 --vcon-forward-once` — retry quickly, never waiting more than 30 s between tries
- `sipnab --vcon-forward spool --vcon-forward-url https://vcon.example.com/v1/vcons --vcon-forward-auth-file vcon.auth --vcon-forward-max-error-body 65536 --vcon-forward-once` — keep up to 64 KiB of each refusal's answer in its `<name>.error.json` record
- `sipnab --vcon-forward spool --vcon-forward-url https://vcon.example.com/v1/vcons --vcon-forward-auth-file vcon.auth --vcon-forward-max-error-body 512 --vcon-forward-max-response-head 16384` — keep 512 bytes of each refusal, and treat an answer whose headers exceed 16 KiB as no answer
- `sipnab --vcon-forward spool --vcon-forward-url https://proxy.example.com/vcon --vcon-forward-auth-file vcon.auth --vcon-forward-max-response-head 131072 --vcon-forward-once` — a store behind a proxy that adds large headers: read up to 128 KiB of them
- `sipnab --vcon-forward spool --vcon-forward-url https://vcon.example.com/v1/vcons --vcon-forward-auth-file vcon.auth --vcon-forward-ca store-ca.pem --vcon-forward-timeout 10` — a store whose certificate a private CA issued: trust only that CA, and give up on a silent store after ten seconds rather than thirty
- `sipnab --vcon-forward spool --vcon-forward-url https://vcon.example.com/v1/vcons --vcon-forward-auth-file vcon.auth --vcon-forward-ca store-ca.pem --vcon-forward-interval 60 --vcon-forward-timeout 120` — a store across a slow link: pass over the spool once a minute and wait up to two minutes for each answer
- `sipnab --vcon-forward spool --vcon-forward-url https://vcon.example.com/v1/vcons --vcon-forward-auth-file vcon.auth --vcon-forward-extra-ca store-ca.pem` — a store whose certificate a private CA issued, on a host whose CA bundle should still count: trust that CA as well as the host's bundle
- `sipnab --vcon-forward spool --vcon-forward-url https://vcon.example.com/v1/vcons --vcon-forward-auth-file vcon.auth --vcon-forward-extra-ca /etc/sipnab/store-ca.pem --vcon-forward-once` — deliver once to such a store and exit
- `sipnab --vcon-forward /var/spool/sipnab-vcon --vcon-forward-url https://vcon.example.com/v1/vcons --vcon-forward-auth-file vcon.auth --vcon-forward-done /var/spool/sipnab-vcon-sent --vcon-forward-failed /var/spool/sipnab-vcon-held --vcon-forward-interval 2` — keep delivered and refused containers beside the spool rather than inside it, on the same file system, and pass every two seconds
- `sipnab --vcon-forward spool --vcon-forward-url https://vcon.example.com/v1/vcons --vcon-forward-auth-file vcon.auth --vcon-forward-replace-url 'https://vcon.example.com/v1/vcons/{uuid}' --vcon-forward-once` — a store that answers `409` for a uuid it holds: PUT the rewritten container to the uuid's own URL instead of filing it as refused
- `sipnab --vcon-forward spool --vcon-forward-url https://vcon.example.com/v1/vcons --vcon-forward-auth-file vcon.auth --vcon-forward-replace-url 'https://vcon.example.com/v1/vcons/{uuid}' --vcon-forward-done sent --vcon-forward-failed held` — the same, polling, with the delivered and refused containers in `sent` and `held`
- `sipnab --vcon-forward spool --vcon-forward-url https://vcon.example.com/v1/vcons --vcon-forward-auth-file vcon.auth --vcon-forward-scitt-url https://ts.example.com --vcon-forward-scitt-sign-key scitt.key --vcon-forward-scitt-sign-cert scitt.crt --vcon-forward-scitt-issuer https://pbx.example.com/sipnab` — register `vcon_created` and `vcon_sent` with the transparency service at `https://ts.example.com/entries` for each container delivered
- `sipnab --vcon-forward spool --vcon-forward-url https://vcon.example.com/v1/vcons --vcon-forward-auth-file vcon.auth --vcon-forward-scitt-url https://ts.example.com --vcon-forward-scitt-auth-file scitt.auth --vcon-forward-scitt-ca ts-ca.pem --vcon-forward-scitt-sign-key scitt.key --vcon-forward-scitt-sign-cert scitt-chain.pem --vcon-forward-scitt-issuer urn:example:pbx-1 --vcon-forward-once` — the same once, to a service that needs a credential and has a certificate from a private CA
- `sipnab --vcon-forward spool --config /etc/sipnab/forward.toml --vcon-forward-scitt-auth-file scitt-rotated.auth --vcon-forward-scitt-ca ts-ca-2026.pem` — take the other forwarder and SCITT settings from the config file, and replace its transparency service credential and CA for this run
- `sipnab --vcon-forward spool --vcon-forward-url https://vcon.example.com/v1/vcons --vcon-forward-auth-file vcon.auth --vcon-forward-content-type application/vcon --vcon-forward-once` — a store that wants the registered vCon media type: send each JSON container as `application/vcon`
- `sipnab --vcon-forward /var/spool/sipnab-vcon --vcon-forward-kind conserver --vcon-forward-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --vcon-forward-auth-file conserver.key --vcon-forward-content-type application/vcon+json` — send each JSON container to a conserver as `application/vcon+json`; a gzip format container still goes as `application/vcon+gzip`
- `sipnab --vcon-spool-status spool` — print how many containers wait in `spool`, how many the forwarder delivered and refused, and the store's answer for each refusal
- `sipnab --vcon-spool-status /var/spool/sipnab-vcon` — the same for a spool given by absolute path; a spool the capture has not written yet prints zeros and `"exists": false`

## vCon fetcher

`--vcon-fetch` runs sipnab as the process that reads stored vCons back from a
store by uuid and writes each to a file.

- It captures nothing.
- sipnab refuses it beside any capture source, listener or export flag, and
  beside `--vcon-forward`.
- The other flags in this section need it.
- Each flag but `--vcon-fetch`, `--vcon-fetch-out` and `--vcon-fetch-overwrite`
  has a `[vcon_fetch]` key in the config file. The flag overrides the key.
- Needs the `vcon` Cargo feature.
- More: [Fetch a stored vCon](@/docs/vcon.md#fetch-a-stored-vcon).

| Flag | Value | Default | Since | Description |
|------|-------|---------|-------|-------------|
| `--vcon-fetch` | `<UUID>...` | -- | 0.5.209 | Read the container with each uuid from the store and write it to `<uuid>.vcon.json` in `--vcon-fetch-out`. `-` reads more uuids from standard input, one per line, and passes over blank lines and lines starting with `#`. The fetcher asks once for a uuid given twice. A uuid is 1 to 64 characters, each a letter, a digit or `-`. Exit `0` when the fetcher wrote every container and the schema accepts each, `1` when it wrote none for some uuid (`404`, another status, a size or shape refusal, a file that exists) or the schema refuses one, `2` when sipnab refuses the settings, `3` when the store answered `401` or `403`: the fetcher then asks for nothing more. Needs a URL and a credential, each from its flag or its `[vcon_fetch]` key; without one sipnab refuses the run with exit `2`, naming both |
| `--vcon-fetch-kind` | `<KIND>` | `generic` | 0.5.209 | The kind of store: `generic`, `vcon-store`, `conserver` or `vcon-mcp`. A kind supplies the read path after the path the URL names, the header when the credential is a bare key, and the removal of what the store wraps around the container. `generic` supplies nothing. The table: [Fetch a stored vCon](@/docs/vcon.md#fetch-a-stored-vcon). Config: `[vcon_fetch] kind` |
| `--vcon-fetch-url` | `<URL>` | -- | 0.5.209 | The store, `http://` or `https://`. With a `--vcon-fetch-kind` other than `generic`, the store's base URL: the kind adds its read path after the path the URL names. The fetcher takes a URL holding `{uuid}` as written, the uuid filled in, for any kind, and the `generic` kind needs one. sipnab refuses credentials in the URL. Plain `http://` to a host other than loopback logs a warning. Config: `[vcon_fetch] url` |
| `--vcon-fetch-auth-file` | `<FILE>` | -- | 0.5.209 | File holding the credential, as the forwarder's auth file does: one `Header-Name: value` line, or, with a `--vcon-fetch-kind` other than `generic`, the bare key, which the kind sends in its header. Refused when other users can read it (`chmod 600` it). A file sipnab cannot read, or one that holds no credential, stops the fetcher with exit 2; the same file named by `[vcon_fetch] auth_file` exits 1. The value never appears in a log line or an error. Config: `[vcon_fetch] auth_file` |
| `--vcon-fetch-out` | `<DIR>` | current directory | 0.5.209 | Where the fetcher writes each container, as `<uuid>.vcon.json`, mode `0600`. The fetcher creates it, mode `0700`, if missing |
| `--vcon-fetch-overwrite` | -- | off | 0.5.209 | Replace a `<uuid>.vcon.json` that exists. Without it the fetcher does not ask the store for that uuid, keeps the file, and exits `1`. Neither form writes through a symbolic link |
| `--vcon-fetch-timeout` | `<SECS>` | `30` | 0.5.209 | Seconds to wait to connect, and for each read and write, before the fetcher gives up on a container, 1 to 600. Config: `[vcon_fetch] timeout` |
| `--vcon-fetch-max-size` | `<BYTES>` | `67108864` | 0.5.209 | The largest answer the fetcher reads for one container, 1 to 4294967295. The fetcher refuses a larger one and writes nothing for it. The default, 64 MiB, holds a container with an hour of inline G.711 audio. Config: `[vcon_fetch] max_size` |
| `--vcon-fetch-max-response-head` | `<BYTES>` | `65536` | 0.5.209 | The most bytes of a store's status line and headers read, 1 to 4294967295. The fetcher refuses an answer with more. Config: `[vcon_fetch] max_response_head` |
| `--vcon-fetch-ca` | `<FILE>` | host bundle | 0.5.209 | Trust only the CA certificates in this PEM file for an `https://` store. Without it the fetcher trusts the host's CA bundle. Config: `[vcon_fetch] ca` |
| `--vcon-fetch-extra-ca` | `<FILE>` | -- | 0.5.219 | Trust the CA certificates in this PEM file for an `https://` store **in addition to** the host's CA bundle: the fetcher accepts the store's certificate when the host's bundle or this file issued it. Use `--vcon-fetch-ca` instead to trust only the named file; the fetcher refuses the two together. Either flag replaces both `[vcon_fetch] ca` and `[vcon_fetch] extra_ca`. Config: `[vcon_fetch] extra_ca` |
| `--vcon-fetch-decrypt-key` | `<FILE>` | -- | 0.5.218 | Decrypt each encrypted container with the RSA private key in this PEM file, verify its signature, and write the unsigned vCon inside. The file must be readable by its owner only. Without it the fetcher writes an encrypted container as the store holds it. See [Fetch an encrypted vCon](@/docs/vcon.md#fetch-an-encrypted-vcon). Config: `[vcon_fetch] decrypt_key` |
| `--vcon-fetch-signer-ca` | `<FILE\|system>` | -- | 0.5.219 | Write a decrypted or signed container only when its signing certificate chains, through the intermediates in its `x5c`, to a CA certificate in this PEM file, with every certificate in the chain within its validity period. `system` uses the host's CA bundle; write `./system` for a file of that name. A container that is not signed has no signer to check and the fetcher writes nothing for it. Needs no key for a signed container; an encrypted one needs `--vcon-fetch-decrypt-key`, and without it the fetcher writes nothing for an encrypted container. See [Check who signed it](@/docs/vcon.md#check-who-signed-it). Config: `[vcon_fetch] signer_ca` |
| `--vcon-fetch-signer-sha256` | `<HEX>` | -- | 0.5.219 | Write a decrypted or signed container only when its signing certificate has this SHA-256 fingerprint: 64 hex digits, plain or in colon-separated pairs, either case, as `openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256` prints it. A container that is not signed has no signer to check and the fetcher writes nothing for it. Needs no key for a signed container; an encrypted one needs `--vcon-fetch-decrypt-key`, and without it the fetcher writes nothing for an encrypted container. Config: `[vcon_fetch] signer_sha256` |

Examples:

- `sipnab --vcon-fetch 018bcfe5-6800-8a6b-a667-78f1c5213800 --vcon-fetch-kind vcon-store --vcon-fetch-url https://api.vcon.store --vcon-fetch-auth-file vcon-store.key --vcon-fetch-out fetched` — read one vCon from vcon.store: the kind adds `/v1/vcons/{uuid}`, sends the key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, and removes the `_meta` member the store adds
- `sipnab --vcon-fetch 018bcfe5-6800-8a6b-a667-78f1c5213800 --vcon-fetch-kind conserver --vcon-fetch-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --vcon-fetch-auth-file conserver.key --vcon-fetch-out fetched` — read one from a self-hosted conserver: the kind adds `/vcon/{uuid}` and sends the key as `x-conserver-api-token`
- `sipnab --vcon-fetch 018bcfe5-6800-8a6b-a667-78f1c5213800 --vcon-fetch-kind vcon-mcp --vcon-fetch-url http://127.0.0.1:3000 --vcon-fetch-auth-file vcon-mcp.key --vcon-fetch-out fetched` — read one from a vcon-mcp server's REST API: the kind adds `/api/v1/vcons/{uuid}`, sends the key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, and keeps the `vcon` member of the answer
- `sipnab --vcon-fetch 018bcfe5-6800-8a6b-a667-78f1c5213800 --vcon-fetch-url 'https://vcon.example.com/store/{uuid}' --vcon-fetch-auth-file vcon.auth --vcon-fetch-out fetched` — a store of no listed kind: the URL template says where the uuid goes, and the auth file holds the full header line
- `sipnab --vcon-fetch - --vcon-fetch-kind vcon-store --vcon-fetch-url https://api.vcon.store --vcon-fetch-auth-file vcon-store.key --vcon-fetch-out fetched < uuids.txt` — read every uuid listed in `uuids.txt`, one per line
- `sipnab --vcon-fetch 018bcfe5-6800-8a6b-a667-78f1c5213800 --vcon-fetch-kind conserver --vcon-fetch-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --vcon-fetch-auth-file conserver.key --vcon-fetch-out fetched --vcon-fetch-overwrite` — read it again, replacing the file an earlier run wrote
- `sipnab --vcon-fetch 018bcfe5-6800-8a6b-a667-78f1c5213800 --vcon-fetch-url 'https://vcon.example.com/store/{uuid}' --vcon-fetch-auth-file vcon.auth --vcon-fetch-ca store-ca.pem --vcon-fetch-timeout 10 --vcon-fetch-max-size 268435456` — a store whose certificate a private CA issued, holding containers up to 256 MiB: trust only that CA, and give up on a silent store after ten seconds
- `sipnab --vcon-fetch 018bcfe5-6800-8a6b-a667-78f1c5213800 --vcon-fetch-url 'https://proxy.example.com/vcon/{uuid}' --vcon-fetch-auth-file vcon.auth --vcon-fetch-max-response-head 131072` — a store behind a proxy that adds large headers: read up to 128 KiB of them
- `sipnab --vcon-fetch 018bcfe5-6800-8a6b-a667-78f1c5213800 --config /etc/sipnab/vcon-store.toml` — take every fetcher setting from a config file's `[vcon_fetch]` section
- `sipnab --vcon-fetch 018bcfe5-6800-8a6b-a667-78f1c5213800 --vcon-fetch-kind vcon-store --vcon-fetch-url https://api.vcon.store --vcon-fetch-auth-file vcon-store.key --vcon-fetch-out fetched --vcon-fetch-overwrite --vcon-fetch-timeout 120` — replace an earlier copy across a slow link, waiting up to two minutes for each read
- `sipnab --vcon-fetch 018bcfe5-6800-8a6b-a667-78f1c5213800 --vcon-fetch-kind conserver --vcon-fetch-url https://conserver.example.com --vcon-fetch-auth-file conserver.key --vcon-fetch-ca conserver-ca.pem --vcon-fetch-max-size 1048576 --vcon-fetch-max-response-head 16384` — a conserver whose certificate a private CA issued, holding containers without inline audio: refuse any answer over 1 MiB, or with more than 16 KiB of headers
- `sipnab --vcon-fetch 018bcfe5-6800-8a6b-a667-78f1c5213800 --vcon-fetch-kind conserver --vcon-fetch-url https://conserver.example.com --vcon-fetch-auth-file conserver.key --vcon-fetch-extra-ca conserver-ca.pem` — a conserver whose certificate a private CA issued, on a host whose CA bundle should still count: trust that CA as well as the host's bundle
- `sipnab --vcon-fetch - --vcon-fetch-kind conserver --vcon-fetch-url https://conserver.example.com --vcon-fetch-auth-file conserver.key --vcon-fetch-extra-ca /etc/sipnab/conserver-ca.pem --vcon-fetch-out fetched < uuids.txt` — fetch every vCon listed in `uuids.txt` from such a store
- `sipnab --vcon-fetch 018bcfe5-6800-8a6b-a667-78f1c5213800 --vcon-fetch-kind conserver --vcon-fetch-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --vcon-fetch-auth-file conserver.key --vcon-fetch-decrypt-key recipient.key --vcon-fetch-out fetched` — read an encrypted vCon from a conserver, decrypt it with the recipient's private key, verify its signature, and write the unsigned vCon
- `sipnab --vcon-fetch - --vcon-fetch-kind conserver --vcon-fetch-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --vcon-fetch-auth-file conserver.key --vcon-fetch-decrypt-key recipient.key --vcon-fetch-out fetched < uuids.txt` — decrypt every vCon listed in `uuids.txt`, one uuid per line; the fetcher writes a container that is not encrypted as the store holds it
- `sipnab --vcon-fetch 018bcfe5-6800-8a6b-a667-78f1c5213800 --vcon-fetch-kind conserver --vcon-fetch-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --vcon-fetch-auth-file conserver.key --vcon-fetch-decrypt-key recipient.key --vcon-fetch-signer-ca signing-ca.pem --vcon-fetch-out fetched` — decrypt a vCon and write it only when the CA in `signing-ca.pem` issued its signing certificate
- `sipnab --vcon-fetch - --vcon-fetch-kind conserver --vcon-fetch-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --vcon-fetch-auth-file conserver.key --vcon-fetch-decrypt-key recipient.key --vcon-fetch-signer-ca system --vcon-fetch-out fetched < uuids.txt` — decrypt every vCon listed in `uuids.txt` and write each only when a CA in the host's CA bundle issued its signing certificate
- `sipnab --vcon-fetch 018bcfe5-6800-8a6b-a667-78f1c5213800 --vcon-fetch-kind conserver --vcon-fetch-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --vcon-fetch-auth-file conserver.key --vcon-fetch-decrypt-key recipient.key --vcon-fetch-signer-sha256 4A:27:CF:DC:D8:87:A5:E5:A9:B5:DE:7E:27:37:C2:48:28:2B:86:44:8A:B3:60:6F:42:99:B2:E2:26:FC:0F:19 --vcon-fetch-out fetched` — decrypt a vCon and write it only when one known certificate signed it
- `sipnab --vcon-fetch 018bcfe5-6800-8a6b-a667-78f1c5213800 --vcon-fetch-kind conserver --vcon-fetch-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --vcon-fetch-auth-file conserver.key --vcon-fetch-decrypt-key recipient.key --vcon-fetch-signer-ca signing-ca.pem --vcon-fetch-signer-sha256 4a27cfdcd887a5e5a9b5de7e2737c248282b86448ab3606f4299b2e226fc0f19 --vcon-fetch-out fetched` — require both: the signing certificate chains to `signing-ca.pem` and has this fingerprint


## vCon archive

`--vcon-resign` re-signs a signed vCon for a long-term archive, as
[draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04 section 5.2.3](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04#section-5.2.3)
describes. It reads one file and writes one, and captures nothing.

| Flag | Value | Default | Since | Description |
|------|-------|---------|-------|-------------|
| `--vcon-resign` | `<FILE>` | -- | 0.5.219 | Re-sign the signed vCon in this file. sipnab verifies every signed layer, requires the outermost signing certificate to be within its validity period now, and signs the file whole, byte for byte, as the payload of a new JWS with the new signer's `x5c` and the vCon's uuid. `--vcon-signer-ca` and `--vcon-signer-sha256` check the input's signer too. Exit `0` when written, `1` when sipnab refuses the input or the output exists, `2` when a key, certificate or signer check does not load. Needs `--vcon-resign-key`, `--vcon-resign-cert` and `--vcon-resign-out`. See [Re-sign for a long-term archive](@/docs/vcon.md#re-sign-for-a-long-term-archive) |
| `--vcon-resign-key` | `<FILE>` | -- | 0.5.219 | The new signer's PEM private key: RSA, which signs `RS256`, or EC P-256, which signs `ES256`. Readable by its owner only |
| `--vcon-resign-cert` | `<FILE>` | -- | 0.5.219 | The PEM certificate chain of `--vcon-resign-key`, leaf first, carried in the new signature's `x5c` |
| `--vcon-resign-out` | `<FILE>` | -- | 0.5.219 | Where sipnab writes the re-signed vCon, mode `0600`. sipnab never replaces a file that exists, and exits `1` instead |

**Examples**
- `sipnab --vcon-resign signed/0158a120-0392-8337-ae55-829bc914b643.vcon.json --vcon-resign-key archive.key --vcon-resign-cert archive.crt --vcon-resign-out archived.vcon.json` — re-sign one signed vCon with the archive's key before its signing certificate expires
- `sipnab --vcon-resign archived.vcon.json --vcon-resign-key archive-2036.key --vcon-resign-cert archive-2036.crt --vcon-resign-out archived-2036.vcon.json` — re-sign the archive again with the next key: the result nests three signed layers
- `sipnab --vcon-resign signed.vcon.json --vcon-resign-key archive.key --vcon-resign-cert archive-chain.pem --vcon-resign-out archived.vcon.json --vcon-signer-ca signing-ca.pem` — re-sign only a vCon whose signer the CA in `signing-ca.pem` issued
- `sipnab --vcon-resign signed.vcon.json --vcon-resign-key archive.key --vcon-resign-cert archive.crt --vcon-resign-out archived.vcon.json --config /etc/sipnab/sipnab.toml` — take the signer checks from the config file's `[vcon_input]` section

## vCon audio fetch

`--vcon-audio-fetch` reads back the audio a `[[vcon.rule]]` with
`audio = "url"` wrote beside its container. It reads one container, fetches
each recording the container names by `url`, and captures nothing.

- It reads the container in any form `-I` reads: unsigned, signed, encrypted or gzip. `--vcon-key`, `--vcon-signer-ca` and `--vcon-signer-sha256`, or their `[vcon_input]` keys, open it.
- sipnab refuses it beside any capture source, listener or export flag, and beside the forwarder, the fetcher, `--vcon-spool-status` and `--vcon-resign`.
- The other flags in this section need it. None has a config key.
- Needs the `vcon` Cargo feature.
- More: [Fetch the audio a vCon names](@/docs/vcon.md#fetch-the-audio-a-vcon-names).

| Flag | Value | Default | Since | Description |
|------|-------|---------|-------|-------------|
| `--vcon-audio-fetch` | `<FILE>` | -- | 0.5.221 | For each recording Dialog Object in this vCon with a `url`: fetch the file over `https://`, check its `content_hash` (draft-ietf-vcon-vcon-core-04 section 2.2) before anything else reads it, decrypt it with `--vcon-key` when it is a JWE, and write the audio to `<uuid>-dialog<N>.wav` or `.ogg` in `--vcon-audio-fetch-out`. sipnab refuses a `url` that is not `https://`, without connecting. Exit `0` when sipnab wrote every recording, `1` when the container does not open, names no recording by `url`, or sipnab refused any recording, `2` when sipnab cannot use a key, CA or output directory. Needs `--vcon-audio-fetch-out` |
| `--vcon-audio-fetch-out` | `<DIR>` | -- | 0.5.221 | Where sipnab writes each recording's audio, mode `0600`. sipnab creates it, mode `0700`, if missing. sipnab never replaces a file that exists: it fetches nothing for that recording, and exits `1` |
| `--vcon-audio-fetch-local` | -- | off | 0.5.221 | Read each recording from the directory that holds the vCon, by the last segment of its `url`, instead of fetching it: for an `--export-vcon-dir` spool whose files your storage does not serve yet. The `content_hash` check still applies |
| `--vcon-audio-fetch-ca` | `<FILE>` | host bundle | 0.5.221 | Trust only the CA certificates in this PEM file for the `https://` server that holds the audio. Without it sipnab trusts the host's CA bundle |
| `--vcon-audio-fetch-extra-ca` | `<FILE>` | -- | 0.5.221 | Trust the CA certificates in this PEM file for the `https://` server that holds the audio **in addition to** the host's CA bundle. sipnab refuses it beside `--vcon-audio-fetch-ca` |
| `--vcon-audio-fetch-max-size` | `<BYTES>` | `67108864` | 0.5.221 | The largest file sipnab reads for one recording, 1 to 4294967295. sipnab refuses a larger one and writes nothing for it. The default is 64 MiB |

**Examples**
- `sipnab --vcon-audio-fetch fetched/0158a120-0392-891a-9455-bc2e6fad94df.vcon.json --vcon-audio-fetch-out audio --vcon-key recipient.key` — fetch, check and decrypt the audio of one encrypted vCon from the storage its `url` names
- `sipnab --vcon-audio-fetch spool/0158a120-0392-891a-9455-bc2e6fad94df.vcon.json --vcon-audio-fetch-out audio --vcon-audio-fetch-local --vcon-key recipient.key` — read the audio from the spool beside the container instead
- `sipnab --vcon-audio-fetch call.vcon.json --vcon-audio-fetch-out audio --vcon-audio-fetch-ca media-ca.pem --vcon-audio-fetch-max-size 268435456` — storage whose certificate a private CA issued, holding recordings up to 256 MiB
- `sipnab --vcon-audio-fetch call.vcon.json --vcon-audio-fetch-out audio --vcon-audio-fetch-extra-ca media-ca.pem` — trust that CA as well as the host's bundle
- `sipnab --vcon-audio-fetch fetched/0158a120-0392-891a-9455-bc2e6fad94df.vcon.json --vcon-audio-fetch-out audio --vcon-key recipient.key --vcon-audio-fetch-ca media-ca.pem` — decrypt the audio of an encrypted vCon from storage whose certificate only that CA issued
- `sipnab --vcon-audio-fetch fetched/0158a120-0392-891a-9455-bc2e6fad94df.vcon.json --vcon-audio-fetch-out audio --vcon-key recipient.key --vcon-audio-fetch-extra-ca media-ca.pem --vcon-audio-fetch-max-size 1073741824` — the same, trusting the host's bundle too, for a recording up to 1 GiB

## G.729 tables (`sipnab g729`)

`sipnab g729` installs and checks the G.729 codebook tables that `--g729-tables` reads. A codebook table is the set of numeric values the G.729 decoder needs. sipnab does not ship them. [G.729 audio](@/docs/g729.md) is the full how-to.

- `sipnab g729 install` downloads the ITU-T G.729 software package, checks its sha256, builds the table file from it and writes the file. It asks before it installs.
- `sipnab g729 status` prints whether the table file holds the tables, the path it read and the hash of the values. It exits `0` when the file holds the tables and `1` when it does not.

Both commands take these options:

- `--g729-tables <PATH>`: the table file, as for a capture run. Without it, `[g729] tables`, else `g729-tables.bin` in the directory of the user config file.
- `-f, --config <FILE>`: the config file to read `[g729] tables` from, as `-f` for a run.
- `--no-config`: read no config file.

`sipnab g729 install` also takes:

- `--yes`: answer yes to the question before installing, for scripts and Dockerfiles.
- `--from <PATH>`: install from the package zip, a directory extracted from it, or the table file of another host, without opening a connection.

**Examples**
- `sipnab g729 status --g729-tables ./g729-tables.bin` — check one table file. With no tables there it prints `G.729 tables: not installed` and `Table file: ./g729-tables.bin`, and exits `1`
- `sipnab g729 status --no-config` — check the default path, `g729-tables.bin` in the directory of the user config file, whatever the config file sets

## Config

| Flag | Value | Default | Since | Description |
|------|-------|---------|-------|-------------|
| `-f`, `--config` | `<FILE>` | -- | 0.3.0 | Path to configuration file (must exist) |
| `-F`, `--no-config` | -- | off | 0.3.0 | Skip loading any configuration file |
| `-D`, `--dump-config` | -- | off | 0.3.0 | Dump effective configuration and exit |
| `--completions` | `<SHELL>` | -- | 0.5.3 | Print a shell completion script (bash, zsh, fish, elvish, powershell) to stdout and exit |

**Examples**

- `sipnab --config /etc/sipnab/sipnab.toml --dump-config` — dump the effective configuration produced by a specific config file, then exit
- `sipnab --no-config --dump-config` — dump the built-in defaults, skipping any configuration file, then exit
- `sudo sipnab -d eth0 --config ~/.config/sipnab/config.toml` — live capture using a per-user configuration file
- `sipnab -N -I capture.pcap --no-config` — analyze an offline pcap with all configuration files ignored
- `sipnab --completions bash > sipnab.bash` — print a bash completion script into a file suitable for /etc/bash_completion.d
- `sipnab --completions zsh > _sipnab` — print a zsh completion script into a file suitable for the zsh fpath


## Validation rules

- Flags that print their answer to stdout require `-N` / `--no-tui` mode, unless `--call-report` or `--export-vcon` is also given: `--json`, `--json-pretty`, `--json-dialogs`, `--report`, `--stun`, `--json-stun`, `--analyze`, `--json-analyze`, `--yang-analyze`, `--hexdump`, `--fail2ban`, `--group-by`, `--wireshark`, `--tshark-filter`, `--recommend-block`, `--lint` and `--vcon-digest`.
- `--kill-response` accepts values 100-699 only.
- Feature-gated flags (`tls`, `hep`, `api`, `mcp`, `mcp-http`) produce startup errors when the required feature is not compiled in.
- `--mcp` refuses every flag in that list, `--call-report`, `--export-vcon` without `--vcon-out`, `--evidence-out -`, and `--relay-stats-interval` on a headless run, because on stdio those would write into the JSON-RPC wire.
  - This holds on every transport, not just stdio.
  - Combine `--mcp` with `--quiet` to suppress text-mode capture output.
- HTTP MCP transport (`--mcp --mcp-transport http`) on a non-loopback `--mcp-bind` requires a bearer token (`--mcp-token` / `--mcp-token-file` / `SIPNAB_MCP_TOKEN`) or a signing key (`--mcp-signing-key` / `--mcp-signing-key-file` / `SIPNAB_MCP_SIGNING_KEY`). Loopback binds need neither.

## Examples

- `sipnab -d eth0` — capture on eth0
- `sipnab -I capture.pcap` — read from pcap file
- `sipnab -N --json -I capture.pcap` — non-interactive JSON output
- `sipnab --problems` — show problematic calls
- `sipnab --kill-scanner -d eth0` — detect SIP scanners
- `sipnab --from alice --to bob` — filter by From/To headers
- `sipnab 'host 192.0.2.1 and port 5060'` — capture filter (BPF): frames that do not match are never read
- `sipnab --filter "method == 'INVITE' AND rtp.mos < 3.0"` — advanced filter DSL
- `sipnab -N -I capture.pcap --call-report "abc123@host" --markdown --no-cli-print` — generate detailed report for a call (drop `--no-cli-print` and the whole capture's message dump precedes it)
- `sipnab -d eth0 -H 192.0.2.50:9060` — capture with HEP mirror
- `sipnab -d eth0 --keylog /tmp/sslkeys.log --keylog-watch` — live TLS decryption

## Exit codes

Scripts can rely on these:

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `0` | Success |
| `1` | Runtime failure — capture error, I/O error, a capture file that was not read in full (a truncated pcap, a member that would not open, a BPF filter that would not compile against one), a `--plugin` that would not load, or sipnab could not produce a requested report (e.g. `--call-report` Call-ID not found). Also a refused configuration: a config file sipnab cannot read, or a value in it sipnab refuses, whichever startup step refuses it |
| `2` | Invalid usage — bad flag value or combination given on the command line, or a flag whose feature is not compiled into this binary. A refusal that a flag takes part in (a flag value, or a pair with one half from a flag and the other from the config file) is this code |
| `3` | Lint gate tripped — `--lint --lint-fail-on <severity>` found a conformance finding at or above that severity. Distinct from `1` on purpose: the tool worked, the CAPTURE is non-conformant. Also an invalid vCon container under `--vcon-validate`, and the vCon forwarder stopping because the store answered `401` or `403` (`--vcon-forward`) |

`--expect` exits with its suite's verdict instead, the `exit_code` its report
carries: `0` every rule that ran passed, `1` a rule failed, `2` no rule ran or
the suite itself is at fault. A run that fails for another reason exits `1`
first, and a tripped `--lint-fail-on` gate exits `3` before the suite's code.

[Error messages](@/docs/errors.md) lists the message sipnab prints with a non-zero
exit code, what it means, and what to do.

A run may read its input in full and stop where you asked it to stop
(`-l/--limit`, `--duration`). It still exits `0`.

- The distinction is whether sipnab failed to do what you asked.
- It is not whether it read everything there was.

### When the answer is partial

`1` says something went wrong.

- It cannot say what.
- A consumer reading `--json-dialogs` on a pipe never sees it at all.

So a run that could not deliver the whole answer also says so in its output:

- **`--json-dialogs`** emits one extra NDJSON line, after the dialogs.
  - The line is under a top-level `sipnab_run` key that no dialog object has.
  - A clean run emits nothing extra.
- **`--report`** ends with an `INCOMPLETE RUN` block naming each reason.

```json
{"sipnab_run":{"input_complete":false,"reasons":["1 of 1 capture file(s) was not read to the end; every report from this run rests on a partial read"],"files":{"given":1,"read_in_full":0,"stopped_early":1,"skipped":0,"not_reached":0},"plugins":{"requested":0,"loaded":0,"failed":0},"retention":{"messages_dropped":0},"archives":{"cut_short":false},"port_gate":{"sip_outside_portrange":0,"sip_outside_ws_ports":0}}}
```

`input_complete` is the same predicate as the exit status. So a script reading
stdout and a script reading `$?` cannot reach different verdicts.

`archives.cut_short` is `true` when sipnab could not unpack an archive `-I`
named to its end. That happens when:

- the archive stops early,
- a header fails its checksum,
- or the walk reaches a ceiling.

Members past that point are in no report. That is data missing from the input.
It fails the run like a truncated file does.

`retention.messages_dropped` counts captured messages that idle compaction
discarded (`[limits] idle_compact_after_secs`).

- It is not a failure: the retention policy did what you configured.

`port_gate` counts SIP that sipnab did not analyze because of the port it used:

- `sip_outside_portrange` for messages with both ports outside `--portrange`,
- `sip_outside_ws_ports` for SIP over WebSocket on a port outside the
  WebSocket port set (`--ws-portrange`).

Like retention, it is not a failure, because the range is what you asked for.
`--report` names either count in its `INCOMPLETE RUN` block. It uses the words
the run summary uses on stderr:

```text
INCOMPLETE RUN — this report does not describe the whole capture:
  - 12 SIP message(s) were seen on ports outside --portrange and were not analyzed; re-run with --portrange 1-65535 to include them
```
